title: Gradient descent
tagline: Step downhill on the loss surface, one lr-sized step at a time.
history: Introduced by Cauchy in 1847; the workhorse behind training most modern ML models.
useCases: Training models with no closed form
When the dataset is too big to invert matrices
whenToUse: A differentiable objective, especially at scale where closed-form is too costly.
whenNotToUse: When a cheap closed form exists, or the objective isn't differentiable.
complexity: O(n·d) per step · make or break: the learning rate
note: The learning rate is everything. At lr = 0.5 it drops to the minimum in one step; past 1.0 it diverges.

code.ruby:
def gradient_descent(w, lr: 0.1, steps: 1000, tol: 1e-8)
  steps.times do
    step = lr * grad(w)
    w -= step
    break if step.abs < tol
  end
  w
end
